subject: psychiatry
title: Disruptive Behavior Disorders, Tourette Syndrome, and Enuresis

steps.tx: **Conduct disorder** is a repetitive and persistent pattern of behavior in children or adolescents in which the basic rights of others or major age-appropriate societal norms and rules are violated. Diagnostic criteria mandate at least three behaviors across four categories: aggression to people/animals, destruction of property, deceitfulness/theft, and serious rule violations.
steps.say: Conduct disorder involves severe violations of societal rules and rights of others, including cruelty to animals, property destruction, and theft.

vis.title: Conduct Disorder Symptom Quadrants
rows: Physical fighting, weapon use, animal cruelty, forced sex
Highest predictor of future adult violent crime
Breaking into houses or cars, shoplifting, conning peers
Truancy before age 13, running away overnight
School expulsion and juvenile justice involvement

steps.tx: **Callous-unemotional traits specifier** in conduct disorder identifies children with limited prosocial emotions, defined by a persistent lack of remorse or guilt, callous lack of empathy, unconcern about school performance, and shallow or deficient affect. This specifier forecasts the highest likelihood of developing adult antisocial personality disorder and severe psychopathy.
steps.say: The callous-unemotional specifier identifies children who lack remorse, guilt, and empathy, forecasting severe adult antisocial personality disorder.

left.title: Childhood-Onset Subtype
points: At least one symptom prior to age 10
Prominent physical aggression and animal cruelty
High rate of comorbid ADHD and low IQ
Strong progression to adult antisocial personality

right.title: Adolescent-Onset Subtype
points: Absence of symptoms before age 10
Driven by deviant peer group socialization
Better preserved empathy and social skills
Higher rate of spontaneous adult remission

steps.tx: **Oppositional defiant disorder**, abbreviated ODD, is characterized by a pattern of angry/irritable mood, argumentative/defiant behavior, or vindictiveness lasting at least six months. Unlike conduct disorder, children with ODD do not physically attack people or animals, do not destroy property, and do not commit theft.
steps.say: Oppositional defiant disorder involves defiant arguing, irritability, and vindictiveness without the severe aggression or property damage of conduct disorder.

left.title: Oppositional Defiant Disorder
points: Frequent loss of temper and touchy mood
Actively defies or refuses adult requests
Deliberately annoys and blames others
No physical violence, theft, or firesetting

right.title: Conduct Disorder
points: Direct violation of basic rights of others
Cruelty to animals and physical fighting
Theft, breaking and entering, arson
Severe lawbreaking and juvenile detention

steps.tx: **Tourette syndrome** is a neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by both multiple motor tics and at least one vocal tic, persisting for more than one year, with onset before 18 years of age. Tics are preceded by a premonitory sensory urge that is temporarily relieved by executing the tic.
steps.say: Tourette syndrome requires multiple motor tics and at least one vocal tic lasting over a year with onset before eighteen, preceded by premonitory urges.

vis.title: Tic Disorder Spectrum
rows: At least one vocal tic present

steps.tx: **Coprolalia and vocal tics** in Tourette syndrome involve vocal productions ranging from simple throat clearing and grunting to complex involuntary utterances of socially unacceptable or obscene words (coprolalia). Sufferers also exhibit echolalia (repeating words of others) and palilalia (repeating one's own words).
steps.say: Vocal tics range from grunting to coprolalia, the involuntary utterance of obscenities, which affects only ten to fifteen percent of Tourette patients.

left.title: Simple Tics
points: Motor: rapid eye blinking, head jerking, nose twitching
Vocal: throat clearing, sniffing, grunting, barking
Involves isolated muscle groups
Brief, meaningless fragments of movement

right.title: Complex Tics
points: Motor: touching objects, squatting, jumping, copropraxia
Vocal: coprolalia (obscenities), echolalia, palilalia
Appears intentional and purposeful
Causes severe social embarrassment and bullying

steps.tx: **Pharmacotherapy for Tourette syndrome** utilizes alpha-2 adrenergic agonists (clonidine, guanfacine) as first-line agents, especially in children with comorbid ADHD. When tics remain severe and disabling, high-potency dopamine D2 receptor antagonists like haloperidol or second-generation agents like aripiprazole and risperidone provide potent suppression.
steps.say: Mild tics are treated with alpha-2 agonists like clonidine. Severe tics require dopamine blockers like haloperidol or aripiprazole.

vis.title: Tourette Pharmacotherapy
rows: First-line in mild tics; treats comorbid ADHD; causes sedation
Preferred atypical antipsychotic; low metabolic risk
FDA-approved; high efficacy; risk of acute dystonia & EPS
Habit reversal training with competing response training

steps.tx: See how the pad under the sheet connects to the alarm box in this picture. The **bell-and-pad alarm** sounds the moment urine completes the circuit, waking the child at the start of voiding. Night after night, that pairing trains waking to a full bladder before wetting occurs, giving the best long-term cure rates for primary nocturnal enuresis when families persist for several weeks.
steps.say: The pad senses the first drops of urine and sounds the alarm. Repeated waking trains the child to respond to a full bladder before wetting the bed.

vis.alt: Bell-and-pad enuresis alarm apparatus with a moisture sensor pad connected to an alarm unit beside a child's bed
vis.caption: Bell-and-pad moisture sensor alarm apparatus used for conditioning treatment of primary nocturnal enuresis. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: **Nocturnal enuresis** is defined as repeated involuntary voiding of urine into bed or clothes, occurring at least twice weekly for three consecutive months in a child at least five years of age. Primary enuresis implies the child has never achieved six months of continuous nocturnal continence.
steps.say: Nocturnal enuresis is bedwetting occurring twice weekly for three months in a child aged five or older who lacks organic urinary pathology.

left.title: Primary Nocturnal Enuresis
points: Never achieved 6 months dry interval
Eighty percent of enuretic cases
Strong genetic linkage (chromosome 12 & 13)
Delayed vasopressin nocturnal surge

right.title: Secondary Enuresis
points: Relapse after at least 6 months of dryness
Triggered by acute psychosocial stress or divorce
Must rule out urinary tract infection
Screen for type 1 diabetes mellitus

steps.tx: **Bell and pad moisture alarm** is the behavioral conditioning treatment of choice for primary nocturnal enuresis, achieving the lowest long-term relapse rate. When the child wets, an electric circuit closes, triggering a loud alarm that awakens the child, conditioning the external urethral sphincter to contract reflexively.
steps.say: The bell and pad alarm is the most effective long-term treatment for bedwetting, conditioning the pelvic floor to wake the child upon wetting.

left.title: Bell and Pad Alarm (Behavioral)
points: Treatment of choice with lowest relapse rate
Requires six to twelve weeks of consistent training
Conditions pelvic floor reflex contraction
High cure rate (>70%) without pharmacotherapy

right.title: Desmopressin (Pharmacological)
points: Synthetic vasopressin V2 receptor agonist
Rapid reduction in nocturnal urine volume
High relapse rate upon medication cessation
Risk of hyponatraemic water intoxication
